claims.proposition_evaluated: On August 26, 2026, Infrastructure Committee rejected administration’s recommended hold on the remaining routes, and City Council had not adopted that hold by September 25, 2026. I applied the brief’s definition of a hold to the declared primary version of Attachment 5.
claims.interpretation_notes: Recommendation 1 asked the committee to recommend an approach to City Council. The minutes do not show a motion to adopt or reject Recommendation 1. Instead, a motion to continue the previously approved scope and advance routes was defeated, 2–2. The committee therefore left Recommendation 1 without a decision under the brief’s rule. Version 2 says the remaining routes will be evaluated and a report will return in Q1 2027 for Council direction; it does not expressly say the listed routes must wait for that step. Thus the proposition fails both at 'rejected' and, under the primary definition, at 'hold.' On the alternative reading that 'did not support' means committee non-adoption alone, that narrower committee-level statement is Supported. City Council as a separate body had not decided Recommendation 1 in the Council minutes supplied through September 16; the full through-September-25 Council record could not be verified, so the Council-body classification is Not established. The minutes show no override: the committee made no substantive decision on item 7.6 for Council to reverse. The previously approved CM-20-0330 scope remained the last documented Council direction, but the failed committee motion did not renew that direction.

supporting_evidence.finding: At item 7.6, A. Salvador moved to continue the programme under the previously approved scope, immediately advance procurement for tender-ready routes, and prepare remaining routes for 2027. A. Salvador and M. Janz voted in favour; E. Rutherford and R. Clarke opposed. It was defeated 2–2. E. Rutherford’s amendment to delete accelerated-construction wording was also defeated 2–2, with the sides reversed. A separate motion to keep Attachment 4 private carried 4–0. No motion on Recommendation 1 was put.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The committee’s motions, named votes and results; neither the continuation motion nor Recommendation 1 carried.

supporting_evidence.finding: The report asks Infrastructure Committee to recommend that City Council approve the approach in Attachment 5 and labels the requested action 'Council decision required.'
supporting_evidence.establishes: Recommendation 1’s text and the body asked to make the final decision.

supporting_evidence.finding: At September 8 City Council item 11.6, a notice requesting future budget options for the listed routes was laid over to October 6. It was neither a motion to adopt Recommendation 1 nor a Council decision on the approach.

challenging_evidence.establishes: The wording of the declared primary approach and why it does not meet the brief’s express-deferral test.

challenging_evidence.finding: The committee defeated the motion whose effect would have been incompatible with Recommendation 1. Defeating that motion did not itself adopt or reject Recommendation 1.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The absence of a committee rejection as defined in the brief.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In IS03688, administration recommended an approach expressly deferring construction or advancement of exactly 14 named, unbuilt programme routes until further evaluation, a report or a decision. Version 2 is the declared primary reading because the agenda and minutes list both replacements without identifying which one governed item 7.6.
claims.interpretation_notes: Recommendation 1 asks for approval of Attachment 5, and all three versions list 13 entries continuing as planned and 14 entries listed apart. Under Version 2, the primary and stricter deferral readings both fail: evaluation and a Q1 2027 report are stated, but the text does not expressly say that advancement waits, that all 14 are removed from scope, or that they will not proceed. The original version differs materially: it expressly removes the 14 entries from the programme for 2026 and 2027, so it meets both deferral readings; its full proposition remains Not established because each route’s construction status could not be verified. Version 1 says listed projects may be revisited and describes conditional removal for routes affecting travel lanes or parking, but does not expressly assign that removal to every one of its 14 listed entries; it fails both readings for the listed set. The verdict is version-sensitive. The 14 entries are: 50 Street (101 Avenue to 109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 Avenue to 101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 Street to 83 Street); 85 Street (93 Avenue to 98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 Street to 96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street); 93 Street (82 Avenue to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street to 89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 Street to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 Avenue to 94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 Street to 163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); Grovenor — 148 Street (Stony Plain Road to 104 Avenue), 104 Avenue (142 Street to 149 Street) and 144 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue). Each is one entry under the brief’s counting rule; splitting joined street segments would increase the count but would change that rule. The 13 continuing entries are: 50 Street (109A Avenue to Goldbar Park Road); 84 Avenue (Mill Creek Ravine to 91 Street); 100 Street (76 Avenue to 80 Avenue); 107 Avenue (East of Groat Road to 163 Street); 110 Avenue/90 Street (92 Street to 112 Avenue) and 112 Avenue (90 Street to 76 Street); 111 Avenue (120 Street to 121 Street); 114 Avenue (81 Street to 89 Street); 127 Avenue (97 Street to 102A Street); 163 Street (87 Avenue to 95 Avenue); 163 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue); 167 Street/169 Street (Whitemud Drive to 87 Avenue); Kingsway (113 Street to 122 Street); Victoria Park Road (116 Street to River Valley Road). Attachment 3 was unavailable, so the status of each of the 14 entries is unresolved for August 10 and August 26, 2026. Their inclusion in an approach described as applying to routes not yet started is an administrative description, not a route-by-route status record.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between the programme’s December 2022 approval and September 25, 2026, Karen Principe or Jennifer Rice moved or seconded at least two defeated City Council motions that each would leave CM-20-0330 with an approved capital budget of $45 million–$55 million and direct the released funds to a named destination.
claims.interpretation_notes: Two separate defeated reductions are documented, with K. Principe moving and J. Rice seconding both; they also meet the stricter co-sponsorship reading. The 2023 amendment reduced a documented $100,000,000 capital budget by $50,000,000, leaving $50,000,000 by my calculation, and expressly identified a reduction in tax-supported debt. The 2024 amendment proposed reductions of $33,650,000 in each of 2025 and 2026: $33,650,000 + $33,650,000 = $67,300,000. From the documented $100,000,000 base, it would leave $32,700,000 by my calculation, outside the primary $45 million–$55 million band. The exact failed part is that both motions would leave about $50 million; only the first would. Both cuts meet the alternative at-least-half reduction rule. The 2024 text identifies tax-supported debt as its funding source but does not expressly redirect money to another named programme, levy, reserve or borrowing reduction. On a strict reading of the destination rule, the alternative-amount classification remains Partially supported; if identifying reduced debt financing counts as directing the released funds to reduced borrowing, it becomes Supported under that alternative only. The December 2024 motion says 'to defund' the project; this describes its proposed cut, not a destination. The contemporaneous budget and cuts are in Canadian dollars.

supporting_evidence.finding: At Fall 2023 budget item 5.1.2, Capital Budget Amendment 2 was moved by K. Principe and seconded by J. Rice. As restated, it proposed reducing CM-20-0330 by $50,000,000, with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt. S. Hamilton, T. Cartmell, J. Rice and K. Principe voted in favour; A. Knack, A. Paquette, A. Sohi, A. Salvador, K. Tang, E. Rutherford, A. Stevenson and J. Wright opposed. It was defeated 4–8; M. Janz did not vote.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City Council Fall 2023 budget minutes, items 5.1.1–5.1.2
supporting_evidence.establishes: The first motion’s operative text, sponsorship, votes and defeat.

It proposed decreasing CM-20-0330 by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026, identifying tax-supported debt as funding. T. Cartmell, J. Rice, E. Rutherford and K. Principe voted in favour; A. Knack, A. Sohi, A. Salvador, M. Janz, K. Tang, A. Stevenson and J. Wright opposed. It was defeated 4–7; S. Hamilton and A. Paquette did not vote.

supporting_evidence.establishes: The second motion’s operative text, sponsorship, votes and defeat.

challenging_evidence.finding: The December 2024 cut totals $67,300,000; against the documented $100,000,000 base it would leave $32,700,000, not $45 million–$55 million. Its operative text does not expressly allocate the released amount to another destination.

limitations: The portal would not open through the web tool. The cited minute items were consulted as carried City text. The September 30, 2024 capital-update figure was available in the search index, but its file could not be opened for a full inspection.

The package supplies selected items from identified candidate meetings, not every City Council minute in the 2022–2026 period. I examined the supplied 2022 budget, 2023 and 2024 fall budget, March and April 2023 borrowing-bylaw, August and September 2025 borrowing-bylaw, and September 2025 suspension items. I could not establish that no further qualifying motion exists elsewhere.

The September 2025 suspension motion was moved by T. Cartmell and seconded by K. Principe and defeated 4–9. It sought to cease construction on a class of bike-lane projects, not to reduce CM-20-0330 to about $50 million.
unknowns: Whether a further qualifying budget motion appears in an unexamined Council meeting.

what_would_change_my_verdict: A second defeated motion jointly brought by Principe or Rice that left $45 million–$55 million in CM-20-0330 and named a destination would make the primary proposition Supported.

A pre-December-2024 approved adjustment establishing a capital budget base of $112,300,000–$122,300,000 would bring that motion’s $67,300,000 cut within the primary remainder band and require recalculation.
